content.text:
The resolver needs explicit peerage alias evidence. The source bridge found locally supports this without surname matching.

Current ownership and failure:

- `funder_name.rs::ParsedPersonName` strips `Lord`, but retains `of Turville`; it does not recognize `Baron`.
- `identity.rs::individual_donor_name` accepts only explicit individual donors and returns the cleaner’s exact parsed name. `classify` requires equality.
- `input.rs::blocking_keys` uses that same function. Both candidate generation and acceptance therefore miss the peerage variants.
- `funder_grouping.rs::ReviewedFamily` operates on persisted identities and contains BBC, GB News, and Premier League. Adding Sainsbury there would conceal the resolver defect and hardcode a person.

Recommended bounded representation:

`PeerageAlias { style, personal_name }`, parsed from a complete source spelling such as `Baron Sainsbury of Turville (David Sainsbury)`.

Build a dataset-level map from exact peerage style to distinct explicit personal names. A style is usable only when its set contains one personal name. Recognize `Lord`/`Baron` through one canonical title representation. Derive these accepted variants from the explicit bridge:

- Exact peerage style, `Sainsbury of Turville`.
- Exact personal name, `David Sainsbury`.
- Expanded peerage form, `David Sainsbury of Turville`, provided the personal name ends with the complete short-style name at a word boundary.

Use the same resolved evidence map for blocking and classification. Preserve the existing generic full-name rule separately. Avoid inserting these contextual identities into the context-free `person_name_normalized` feature.

Required negative cases include Francesca Sainsbury, Francesca Sainsbury Perrin, a different territorial designation, conflicting explicit aliases for one style, occupational parentheticals, malformed parentheses, companies, unknown donor kinds, and payer roles. Short peerage plus plain personal name without an explicit bridge must remain unresolved. Ambiguity must prevent short-style attachment rather than joining competing people transitively.

A reviewed registry could establish identities without a bridge but would need curated external evidence and ongoing ownership. Generic territorial stripping or surname projection gives weaker evidence than the available source and should be rejected.

Runtime verification can extend `individual_donor_title_variants_resolve_to_one_identity_per_person` in `exposed/tests/declaration_resolution_cli.rs`. Include both parenthetical spellings, both reported peerage spellings, plain David, and the negative names. Assert one David identity, separate negatives, preserved source names, unchanged cleaned artifacts, preserved funding occurrences, and donor attribution. Run the existing clean/resolve CLI test, then resolve a copied retained capture and load into an isolated database to check actual funder pages. Resolution refuses to overwrite an existing bundle.

One existing verification defect needs repair. `.agents/skills/funder-identity/kani/src/lib.rs::observation` omits `person_name_normalized`, which #136 added to `Observation`. Add `None` before running `check.py`. New domain fields or modules also require corresponding canonical extraction/include changes in `kani/build.rs`; do not reproduce production matching logic in the harness.

No files were changed and no tests were run.
